criteria.evidence: Turn 0 survey misidentified the repo as 'pg2ch', a PostgreSQL→ClickHouse CDC tool, and proposed generic features (Distributed Table Sink, DLQ) not tied to any open issue or the actual faucet-stream code; reply was also truncated and ended with a stray 'duplicate background notification' note.

Replay said gh was unavailable and drafted a 'Progress update — Oct 2026' comment listing recent commits, but did not produce updated epic body text or identify stale/shipped items in #38 as the user asked ('show me what you'd change in the issue body').
Turn 2 reply presents the draft and summarises 'That covers what shipped, what the CI gate now enforces, and aligns the next items with the roadmap.'

Diff adds pub fn validate() to Csv/Duckdb/Elasticsearch/Gcs/Graphql configs checking trim().is_empty() on required fields and validate_batch_size, returning FaucetError::Config, wired into each constructor.
CsvSource::new/GraphqlStream::new now call config.validate()? (returning Result), Duckdb/Elasticsearch/Gcs new() call validate()?; validate tests pass (5/5/6/4/6).

Only cargo check and `cargo test ... -- validate` are shown; no clippy, docs, semver-checks, CLI builds, schema check or coverage run, and changing CsvSource::new/GraphqlStream::new from -> Self to -> Result is a public API break semver-checks would flag.
Final message summarises code changes only; no commit, branch, PR attempt, or report of PR state/what remains and why.

judge.reason: The replay's initial recommendation was grounded in a hallucinated project description rather than the repo's issues or code, and it never attempted or reported on a PR, nor ran the repository's CI checks despite introducing a breaking constructor signature change. The validate() implementation itself is sound and tested, but multiple non-withdrawn criteria (c1, c2, c5, c6) are unmet.
